Find My engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Find My stack covers storefront language. Developer portal, accessory certification, and Connect actually separate item-tracking behavior from product-page copy:

  • Find My network accessory program — MFi certification, accessory firmware, and pairing flows for third-party trackers. Controls whether hardware participates in the Find My network. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • Nearby Interaction & UWB (U1) — precision-finding ranging between iPhone and supported accessories. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains item location to buyers.
  • CoreLocation & background location — GPS, geofencing, and location permission prompts in the binary. Your listing may mention last-known location; wiring location APIs is engineering work, not listing copy.
  • Accessory setup firmware — onboarding flows for tags, fobs, and Find My-compatible hardware. Configuring pairing is engineering — AppLocale does not touch it.
  • MapKit — map views, annotations, and routing UI inside your app. Find My listing copy markets item tracking and Lost Mode; MapKit listing copy markets navigation maps — see MapKit guide for that scope.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Find My capability flags in the binary.

A working Find My integration and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe Find My, AirTag-style tracking, and Lost Mode on the product page in zh-Hans, not how you implement accessory firmware or UWB ranging in code.

Find My-specific vocabulary — what translates differently in zh-Hans

Item-tracking listings use terms general localization guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers evaluate Find My features — not a literal paste of US marketing:

查找 (Find My) vs 查找网络 (Find My network)

Apple's Chinese system UI uses 查找 for the Find My app and ecosystem. 查找网络 fits when your marketing emphasizes crowdsourced network tracking — millions of Apple devices helping locate lost items. Pick the term buyers recognize on each screenshot frame — a Find My app icon frame needs 查找-friendly phrasing; a network-coverage map may use 查找网络 when accurate.

AirTag as brand vs generic item tracking

Apple keeps AirTag as a product name in Chinese marketing alongside 查找-compatible accessories. If your app supports third-party Find My network tags but not Apple AirTag specifically, zh-Hans copy should say 兼容查找网络的追踪器 or 第三方物品追踪 — not imply you ship Apple AirTag hardware. AppLocale rewrites from your stated accessory matrix and English claims.

丢失模式 (Lost Mode) and 精确查找 (precision finding)

US pages use Lost Mode for lock-and-alert workflows and precision finding for UWB arrow guidance. Chinese App Store copy commonly uses 丢失模式 for Lost Mode and 精确查找 for precision finding when your app or accessory actually supports those surfaces. Do not promise 精确查找 in listing copy if your product only shows last-known map pins without UWB ranging.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need Find My-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 查找, 查找网络, 丢失模式, and 追踪物品 each signal different intent from generic location or map keywords.

Common mistakes on Find My-themed zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming Find My integration localizes automatically — accessory paired in the app; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and Find My screenshot caption lines still English
  • Conflating Find My with MapKit navigation — listing says "turn-by-turn directions" when the product story is item tracking, not route planning
  • Promising AirTag when you ship third-party tags only — zh-Hans copy implies Apple AirTag hardware when Connect and your binary support only certified third-party accessories
  • English Lost Mode on zh-Hans screenshots — Connect caption fields are Chinese but burned-in badges on PNG exports are still Latin
  • Expecting AppLocale to implement Find My network firmware — accessory engineering and MFi certification are outside listing rewrite scope
  • What's New still English after Find My launch — see What's New in Simplified Chinese when tracking features shipped in a recent version

Does integrating Find My auto-translate my China listing?

No. Find My network accessories, location APIs, and Lost Mode UI control in-app behavior — they do not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback even when screenshots show Find My in English.

Find My listing copy markets item location, Find My network tracking, AirTag-style find workflows, and Lost Mode — 查找 and 查找网络. MapKit copy markets in-app maps and navigation. Handoff copy markets session resume across devices (接力). Different buyer story, different zh-Hans vocabulary.
